ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC, OFAC, United Nations Security Council, Canada's Consolidated Special Economic Measures Act (CEMA), and Canadian Criminal Code terrorism financing lists. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), close associates, or persons resident in high-risk jurisdictions. All screenings must be documented and retained for at least five years post-relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be presented in English, French, or a combined English-French form using the standard Latin alphabet. Non-Latin transliteration requires a formal English/FRench transliteration and may be rejected if indistinguishable from an existing name. Permitted characters are Roman letters (A-Z), Arabic numerals (0-9), and limited punctuation such as periods, commas, and ampersands. Designations such as 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' must comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected by the Director under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of rejection. The appeal must state the basis of prejudice, provide a NUANS name search report, and propose a revised name. The Director will reconsider the application and issue a final determination within 30 days. Alternatively, a fresh name reservation may be submitted with a new NUANS search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally permitted for non-licensed software publishing activities, but a physical registered office address in Alberta must be lawfully designated and capable of receiving service of process during normal business hours. A virtual office may be used if it provides actual reception services and a rental address; a bare mailbox service without physical presence may be rejected. The registered office must be staffed or have a registered agent authorized to accept legal process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection is approximately 5% for non-licensed software publishers operating through a compliant virtual office and maintaining a physical registered agent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 5-7 on incorporation and articles, section 15 on unlimited shareholder liability, sections 102-119 on directors and officers, and section 20 on registered office and records office requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent or the Alberta Business Registry platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, Alberta Corporate Registry Form 1, expressly stating that shareholder liability is unlimited, together with the registered office, records office, share structure, director information, and agent-for-service information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. No statutory escrow account is required. Subscribers must take and pay for the issued shares in accordance with the subscription terms and the corporation's articles. The corporation should maintain evidence of payment and its securities register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept the subscription of [Subscriber] for [number and class] shares at [price] per share, payable in cash or other lawful consideration, and that the shares be issued upon receipt and recorded in the securities register. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office and records office be established at [Alberta address], with [agent] appointed as agent for service where required. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [names] are appointed President, Secretary, Treasurer, and authorized signing officers, each authorized to execute incorporation, banking, tax, licensing, and ordinary-course documents. The officers shall maintain all statutory registers and records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Corporate Name and Confirm ULC Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent; Alberta NUANS name-search system where a word name is used.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an Alberta NUANS report if required for the proposed word name, confirm that the name is not confusingly similar or prohibited, and prepare articles that expressly provide for unlimited shareholder liability. A numbered corporation may be used if name reservation is unnecessary. Confirm that the proposed social-casino software will not involve real-money wagering, cash-equivalent prizes, or consideration-based gaming.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office address in Alberta
Identification and authority documents for incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select an available numbered name or obtain a revised NUANS report and resubmit. If the ULC provision is omitted, file articles of amendment before issuing shares or otherwise correct the articles through the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry service counter or authorized registry agent; Alberta Business Registry online channel where supported.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation application, Form 1 Articles of Incorporation, prescribed fee, and supporting name documentation. Ensure the registered office and records office are physical Alberta addresses and that the articles clearly state unlimited shareholder liability. Registry filings generally do not require notarization; foreign execution documents should be certified or notarized where requested by the registry agent.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to registry deficiencies through the filing agent, correct the form or attachments, and resubmit without changing the corporation's intended ULC status. Retain the certificate of incorporation and filed articles in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors; Alberta Corporate Registry for subsequent statutory changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting or execute written board resolutions. Adopt the registered and records office, approve share subscriptions and issuance, appoint officers, authorize banking and tax registrations, approve the fiscal year-end, adopt signing authorities, and establish the securities register, central securities register, minute book, and beneficial-ownership register required under applicable law.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or organizational minutes
Proof of consideration paid for issued shares
Securities register and share certificate or uncertificated-share record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt corrective resolutions, replace incomplete registers, and file articles or notices of change where a statutory detail was inaccurately reported. Keep an audit trail showing the original error, correction date, and approving authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, Payroll, and Business Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online and Alberta tax authorities, as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and register for GST/HST when required or voluntarily elected. Register payroll accounts before employing personnel. Assess corporate income-tax filing, non-resident withholding, transfer-pricing, treaty, and ULC classification consequences before making any tax election. Register for Alberta corporate tax administration where required through the applicable federal process.
required_dossiers: Business activity description and expected revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inaccurate CRA information through Business Registration Online or CRA correspondence channels. File any missed returns, elections, or remittances promptly and obtain professional advice before relying on pass-through, treaty, or hybrid-entity treatment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Gaming, Consumer, Privacy, and Platform Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis; Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta; Competition Bureau; Apple App Store and Google Play policy-review systems.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Document that the product is simulated entertainment and does not permit wagering, cash-out, cash-equivalent prizes, or other regulated gaming features. Review provincial gaming legislation and obtain written regulatory advice if monetization changes. Implement privacy, consent, age-rating, advertising, consumer-protection, virtual-item, refund, and platform-payment controls before launch.
required_dossiers: Terms of use and virtual-currency terms
Apple and Google platform compliance records
Regulatory classification opinion, if features are borderline
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Suspend the affected feature, revise the mechanics or disclosures, and seek AGLC or legal clarification before relaunch. Appeal platform rejection through the applicable review process and preserve all compliance evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No Alberta industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for software publishing and simulated social-casino game development. Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis must be consulted if the product includes real-money wagering, regulated lottery activity, cash-equivalent prizes, or other gaming conduct.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating permit for software publishing. A municipal business licence, development permit, occupancy approval, or home-business approval may be required by the municipality where operations are conducted.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary software development and office operations with no industrial facility, resource activity, significant emissions, wastewater discharge, or hazardous-material handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, industrial VOC emissions, or manufacturing waste is expected. Municipal wastewater, waste, recycling, electronic-waste, hazardous-material, and building requirements remain applicable where relevant. Any data-centre or physical production facility must be separately assessed under applicable Alberta and federal environmental rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No sector-specific civil-defence clearance is ordinarily required for office-based software operations. The operator must comply with municipal fire-code, occupancy, building, and emergency-planning requirements, including inspection by the local authority having jurisdiction where requested. Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation applies to employees, including workplace hazard assessment, incident reporting, training, and safe-work procedures. Structural-load and building inspections are required only where the premises, equipment, alterations, or occupancy classification triggers them.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll and import/export accounts via the Business Registration Online portal and GST/HST NETFILE; Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) for Alberta corporate income tax. Alberta has no provincial sales tax or separate provincial sales tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation of the Alberta ULC under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), obtain a federal Business Number (BN) using CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1, selecting the Corporation Income Tax, GST/HST, Payroll and Import/Export accounts as applicable; then register with the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration for Alberta corporate tax. Deliverables include certified constitutional documents, Alberta certificate of incorporation, registered office information, director/officer details, and unlimited-liability share terms for the non-resident owner. The CRA will issue a separate GST/HST program account number under the BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box election exists. The Alberta ULC is a separate taxable corporation for Canadian federal and Alberta income tax purposes. For U.S. federal tax purposes only, a single-owner ULC may be eligible to elect disregarded status under U.S. Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-3 using Form 8832; Canada does not adopt that foreign classification. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules under Income Tax Act sections 18.2 and 18.4 may recharacterize expenses or income arising from hybrid entities. Other domestic elections include section 85 rollover elections and amalgamation/winding-up elections. A Canadian-controlled private corporation election is unavailable to a 100% non-resident-owned ULC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) - federal value-added tax; Alberta applies the 5% federal GST only, with no provincial component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (small-supplier threshold: a person carrying on business in Canada must register once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 in any calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive quarters; non-resident digital suppliers of gaming/app content are subject to the same threshold for supplies made to Canadian recipients).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a national real-time fiscal clearance regime, digital stamping system, or mandatory continuous transaction control (CTC) API e-invoicing mandate. GST/HST returns are self-filed electronically through NETFILE. Invoices must include the information prescribed by the Excise Tax Act; electronic invoices and digital records are acceptable. CRA may perform transaction-level analytics and document matching; Apple IAP and Google Play payment reconciliations are not tax clearances and do not replace statutory invoicing and record-keeping obligations. Quebec's separate QST electronic invoicing and filing requirements do not apply in Alberta.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The ULC may claim 0% GST/HST on qualifying export supplies: (i) tangible goods physically exported from Canada with required customs documentation; and (ii) digital supplies of software licences, virtual slots/social casino content, and related services supplied to a non-resident recipient outside Canada, provided the supply is not for use or consumption in Canada. The exporter must demonstrate the recipient's non-resident status through contracts, payment routing, intellectual-property delivery data, and app-store/platform sales evidence. Zero-rated export supplies allow full input tax credit recovery and net GST/HST refund claims.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the Canada Export Reporting System (CERS) where physical goods or software media are shipped
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier delivery proof for physical export shipments
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT confirmation, bank statement, or platform payout reconciliation evidencing foreign-currency proceeds
Executed international software/supply licence agreement identifying the non-resident customer, jurisdiction, and use rights
Non-resident tax status evidence (e.g., CRA Form NR301, U.S. Form W-8BEN-E, or foreign tax residence certificate)
Digital delivery logs, server/IP records, and Apple IAP/Google Play reports proving delivery to non-resident end users
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating by tracing the full contract-to-payment-to-delivery chain, especially for digital gaming exports. Inadequate substantiation results in reassessment at 5% GST/HST, disallowance of input tax credits and refunds, clawback of prior net-tax refunds, interest, and penalties. Gross negligence penalties under subsection 285(1) of the Excise Tax Act are the greater of C$250 and 50% of the net tax; wilful evasion may trigger criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act and Income Tax Act. Unrepatriated export proceeds beyond the 180-day benchmark are an audit red flag and may lead to recharacterization of the supply as taxable Canadian consumption, with penalty and arrears interest assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). The Minister of Finance and the Department of Finance Canada retain residual exchange-control policy authority under the Currency Act, the Financial Administration Act, the Special Economic Measures Act, and the United Nations Act. Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control permit office, consistent with its IMF Article VIII liberalised open-currency status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada imposes no exchange controls and grants full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the Canadian dollar (CAD). No approval, permit, prior declaration, or licensing requirement applies to inward investment layers, dividend or branch-profit remittances, royalty and management-fee payments, or repayment of shareholder loans. Profit remittance hurdles are exclusively tax and reporting oriented: non-residents are subject to Part XIII withholding tax of 25% statutorily (frequently reduced to 5-15% under the Canada-United States Income Tax Convention and other tax treaties) on dividends, interest, royalties, rents, and management fees, with mandated NR4 returns and remittances to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). Cross-border funds movement is subject to FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting by financial institutions for each international EFT of CAD 10,000 or more in a 24-hour period, and to sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists. A transfer may be blocked, delayed, or rejected where the counterparty, currency route, intermediary bank, or ultimate beneficiary is sanctioned. Alberta imposes no provincial currency controls, remittance restrictions, capital controls, or separate exchange-approval body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has not required export-proceeds surrender since the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations in 1951. There is no statutory holding period, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to channel export receipts through the domestic banking system. Receipts from simulated social-casino revenue through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing may be retained in USD or converted to CAD at the corporate treasury's discretion. For goods exports, a B13A export declaration is required through the Canadian Export Reporting System for controlled, regulated, or high-value goods purely for customs and statistical purposes, not for FX surrender; services and royalty flows are captured through Statistics Canada survey requirements. FINTRAC EFTR obligations apply to the financial institution, not to the exporter, for each international EFT of CAD 10,000 or more within a 24-hour period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low (conditionally viable as an offshore treasury-concentration vehicle, not as a Canadian payment rail). Canada does not issue electronic-money-institution (EMI) licences under the UK or EU model; payment services are regulated under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), administered by the Bank of Canada, and a payment service provider that operates in or targets Canada must be registered with the Bank of Canada. An offshore digital EMI (for example, an FCA-authorised UK EMI or an EU e-money institution) cannot lawfully provide payment services to Canadian residents or to the ULC's Canadian treasury operations without RPAA registration, and Canadian tier-1 banks will generally decline to credit or settle accounts for an unregistered offshore EMI. The EMI may nevertheless serve as an offshore USD concentration node where Apple/Google marketplace payouts are collected and then remitted to the ULC's Schedule I operating account, provided that: (i) no Canadian end-user payment services are rendered by the EMI; (ii) balances are not held as client money in a manner that triggers Canadian insolvency, securities, or banking regulation; (iii) the board expressly accepts the absence of Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) protection and the lack of Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) prudential oversight; and (iv) every onward transfer carries a clear purpose code and full audit trail. Conservative treasury practice is to hold all marketplace proceeds directly in a USD or CAD account at a Canadian Schedule I bank and use offshore EMIs only for non-Canadian developer and advertising settlements where bank correspondent access is constrained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a statutory requirement under FINTRAC, but bank policy for a medium-risk-enhanced gaming-adjacent ULC will in practice require: (i) a live video interview with the compliance officer for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; and (ii) a physical account-opening session in an Alberta branch for at least one Canada-resident director or authorised signatory. Non-resident directors may complete remote identity verification through FINTRAC-compliant electronic methods (secure video conferencing with government-issued credential validation) or through a commissioned notary or approved KYC agent in their home jurisdiction, coupled with notarially certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and apostilled corporate documents. Remote opening is therefore permitted for non-resident directors, but the ULC must present a physical signatory or a registered Alberta agent to authenticate corporate records, execute the banking resolution, and receive security tokens, cheque stock, or digital-banking hardware.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation structure combined with a US 'check-the-box' disregarded-entity election, creating ambiguity as to the true account holder, the governing taxation classification, and underwriting concern about unlimited shareholder liability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation or amalgamation; current provincial registry abstract; articles, by-laws, unanimous shareholders' agreement, and complete shareholder register; Form 8832 entity-classification election filed with the US Internal Revenue Service; board resolution naming signatories and the treasury mandate; UBO declaration for every direct and indirect shareholder holding 10% or more; and a Canadian legal-opinion letter confirming that the ULC is validly constituted, that bank deposits are obligations of the bank rather than of shareholders, and that unlimited shareholder liability does not impair the bank's claim or security priority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived gambling component in the social-casino and virtual-slots product description, triggering banking reputational-risk and merchant-processing exclusion policies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Canadian gaming counsel confirming that simulated social-casino products with no real-money wagers, no cash-out, no redeemable in-game value, and no permitted secondary market fall outside the definition of 'gaming' under section 197(1) of the Criminal Code and therefore require no AGCO iGaming licence; Apple App Store and Google Play policy approval records (Apple guideline 4.7 and Google gambling-equivalent and real-money-gambling policy compliance); audited game and virtual-currency design documentation; age-gating and geo-blocking controls for prohibited territories; certified independent audit report confirming no real-money disbursement or virtual-chip conversion; and the ULC's anti-money-laundering and anti-terrorist-financing programme with transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction-reporting procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity small-value digital payments from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing and recurring USD-to-CAD conversion, creating the risk that the ULC is treated as a money-services business (MSB) or payment service provider requiring registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC MSB assessment file or reasoned legal memorandum confirming that the ULC acts solely as the merchant of record receiving platform payouts and does not perform money transfers, remittance services, third-party currency exchange, or virtual-currency redemption; executed Apple and Google developer contracts demonstrating that the platforms process, collect, and settle all player funds; 30-, 60-, and 90-day cash-flow projections with bank reconciliation statements; month-end platform settlement statements tied to a registered merchant ID; and documented sanctions-screening, transaction-monitoring, and SAR policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injections from US parent shareholders (USD to CAD) flagged as potential layering, structuring, or thin-capitalisation planning.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital call notices, subscription agreements, and shareholder loan agreements; source-of-wealth certificate and bank statements from the remitting US parent; board resolutions authorising each injection; audited opening balance sheet of the ULC; CRA filings including Form T106 information returns for non-resident-controlled corporations where applicable; thin-capitalisation ratio analysis under subsection 18(4) of the Income Tax Act preserving the 1.5:1 debt-to-equity safe harbour; and a coupon and interest schedule with Part XIII withholding position for any intercompany debt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to a diffuse network of foreign software developers, game studios, ad-technology vendors, and affiliate marketers, creating unexpected-payee scrutiny and correspondent-bank friction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor onboarding file with KYC/UBO information for each payee; executed agreements containing deliverables, milestones, invoicing, and payment terms; approved-payee master list requiring exact-name matching of SWIFT BIC and beneficiary account; purchase orders and goods-and-services receipts; ISO 20022 purpose codes on MT103 instructions (for example, ROYL for royalties, LICF for licensing fees, and applicable services-purpose codes); duplicate-payment and sanctions-screening audit logs; and transfer-pricing documentation substantiating arm's-length service fees and software royalties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections, comprising equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, and intercompany treasury advances, must be originated as SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires to the ULC's designated operational or capital-escrow account using the exact legal name and account number registered in the Alberta banking file. Free-text field 70 of the MT103 should carry purpose descriptors such as 'EQUITY INJECTION', 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN', or 'INTERCOMPANY FUNDING', and, where the receiving bank accepts ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose codes, use 'INTC' for intercompany payments, 'EQUI' for equity-related financing, or the bank's specified capital-contribution code; generic descriptions such as 'TRANSFER' must be avoided. Prior to each inbound wire, the ULC must provide the relationship manager with a board resolution or capital-call notice, the subscription or shareholder-loan agreement, a source-of-funds certificate from the remitting US parent's bank, and a funding schedule identifying currency (USD or CAD). The receiving financial institution will apply FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting for international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more in a 24-hour period and OSFI- and Global Affairs Canada-compliant sanctions screening; no prior regulatory approval is required for foreign direct investment, but the ULC must complete Statistics Canada inward-investment surveys when notification thresholds are triggered.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails are bifurcated. Domestic Canadian disbursements, including payroll, Alberta-based hosting providers, and Canadian vendors, clear through Payments Canada infrastructure (ACSS and real-time rails) and Interac e-Transfer for small amounts. Cross-border vendor, developer, and platform disbursements must be remitted via SWIFT MT103, with MT202 COVER for the USD correspondent-leg routing, using exact beneficiary BIC and account-number matching and appropriate purpose codes (royalties, licensing fees, software services, advertising services) to avoid compliance holds. Where a software or advertising vendor requires documentary security or prepayment protection, the Alberta branch may issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600, with electronic delivery or acceptance certificates replacing transport documents because software and virtual-goods deliverables are intangible; standby letters of credit under ISP98 may be used as performance bonds. For Apple and Google payout concentration, the ULC should maintain a segregated USD account, instruct the app stores to settle net revenue to that account under a merchant ID matching the bank KYC file, and execute USD-to-CAD conversion through the bank's treasury desk under pre-agreed spot or forward pricing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable outright forwards, plain-vanilla and non-speculative, fully documented under an ISDA Master Agreement and the Canadian Master Agreement for Treasury Derivatives, and sized against forecast Apple/Google payout inflows.
CAD/USD foreign exchange swaps, simultaneously pairing a spot and forward transaction on equivalent notionals for liquidity conversion and temporary USD deployment without interest-rate risk.
CAD/USD cross-currency swaps, available for long-dated intercompany loans and semi-annual USD cash-flow matching, subject to board-approved derivative-risk policy and ISDA/CSA documentation.
Zero-premium collars and vanilla CAD/USD options, permissible where the treasury policy authorises option-based protection, with premiums expensed transparently and no naked option-writing.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible or practicable for CAD: the Canadian dollar is a fully convertible deliverable currency with an active onshore market, and Canadian Schedule I banks will not routinely write CAD NDFs. Any NDF-like structure lacking physical settlement would be treated as speculative and rejected by internal treasury-risk committees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the corporation's anniversary date of registration or last annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late filing penalty per year; continued non-filing for 2 consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off or dissolution by Alberta Corporate Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (T2) including Alberta corporate tax request schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeated default may result in legal assessment, certified lien, or dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (TBD if annual filer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, within 3 months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 1% to 0.1% of net taxable sales plus 6% interest compounded daily; refundable credits may be withheld

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the corporation is a distributing corporation, publicly accountable, subject to securities regulator requirement, or a shareholder owning at least 5% of issued voting shares requests an audit. Private non-distributing ULC is exempt if all members waive audit in a written annual resolution
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook Part I (IFRS) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private unlimited liability corporations may elect Part II (ASPE) or voluntary IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An internal annual UBO confirmation must be prepared at each fiscal year-end. Directors must confirm beneficial owners holding 25% or more of shares or control rights, update registers for any share transfers, and record the confirmation in the minute book. Alberta does not currently require a separate provincial UBO filing for non-distributing corporations, but the corporation's registered office and records must be maintained in Alberta

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 for a small ULC under ASPE

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined statutory general corporate rate (15% federal Canada Revenue Agency general rate + 8% Alberta provincial general corporate rate); the Canadian-controlled private corporation small-business deduction is unavailable because the ULC is non-resident-controlled.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for software publishing in Alberta; available tax incentives include the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit at 15% (non-refundable for a non-CCPC), 100% immediate capital cost allowance on eligible software under CCA Class 12, and normal business deductions for licensed third-party content; Alberta does not currently provide a patent box or digital media credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through approved electronic EFILE software or the CRA's Secure Electronic Services Portal; Alberta corporate income tax is administered federally under a tax collection agreement, so a single T2 return also assesses the Alberta 8% corporate tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations with a federal balance due exceeding C$3,000 must pay quarterly tax instalments, but the T2 return itself is filed once per taxation year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return is due no later than six months after the stated taxation year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following year). The final balance of federal and Alberta corporate tax is due two months after the taxation year-end for a non-CCPC ULC; interest is charged daily on any late balance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Corporation Legal Name and BN
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the exact Alberta-registered ULC legal name and the CRA Business Number (RP or RC account) assigned on incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners should use the Canadian ULC's official CRA corporation number; never use a U.S. personal social insurance number or U.S. EIN as a substitute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the tax year-end date, which normally must match the ULC's financial accounting period and is commonly December 31.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A ULC is resident in Canada and must file on a full-calendar-year basis unless a CRA-permitted alternative year-end is obtained before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing after store fees but before royalty and platform costs; disclosure of gross versus net receipt treatment is required for virtual gaming transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide revenue if the ULC is centrally managed in Alberta; for Canadian tax purposes the corporation's residence governs taxation scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim CCA on acquired software, intangibles, servers, and licences using prescribed CCA classes and half-year rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident-owned ULC, CCA can be claimed only for eligible property used in the Canadian business activities; ensure Form T2208 (depreciation) is completed in Canadian dollars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable income, including transfer-pricing adjustments, foreign accrual property income (FAPI), and non-deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An Alberta ULC is not eligible for Non-Resident-Owned Investment Corporation (NROIC) status; ordinary Part I rules and Part XIV branch tax apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the combined federal and Alberta provincial corporate tax at 15% and 8%; apply any treaty credits and non-creditable foreign surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute two-country effective rates and claim only treaty-residence-based reductions; if the ULC is fiscally transparent for U.S. purposes, still make the Canadian return in the ULC's own name.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under Income Tax Act s.162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% for each full month up to 12 months; where no tax is outstanding, a minimum penalty of C$100 may apply; gross negligence penalties under s.163(2) can be 50% of understated tax. CRA also charges daily compound statutory interest on unpaid balances and may issue a demand to file or a court order.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding under Income Tax Act s.212(2) on dividends paid by the Alberta ULC to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 5% under the Canada-US Income Tax Convention for a U.S. corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the voting stock for a 365-day period, otherwise to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the ULC before payment with a completed CRA Form NR302 (Application for a Reduction of Tax on Investment Income) together with a Canadian/US Certificate of Tax Residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166) or the applicable treaty country's residence certificate. If tax was over-withheld, a refund is obtained through CRA Form NR301 and a supporting treaty claim. The beneficial owner must satisfy the Canada-US treaty's limitation-on-benefits clause and report the dividend in its home jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding for payments of IP royalties to a non-resident is 25% Part XIII; under the Canada-US treaty royalties are generally 0% where the beneficial owner is a U.S. resident and the amount is arm's length. Interest paid to arm's-length non-resident lenders is generally exempt from Part XIII under the domestic arm's-length interest exemption; non-arm's-length interest is subject to 25% statutory withholding, reduced to 0% under the Canada-US treaty for non-arm's-length interest not dependent on profits, and to 15% where excessive or participating.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not prescribe a universal absolute C$ threshold for Local File/Master File preparation; however, CRA administrative guidance requires contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation where the aggregate fair market value of non-arm's-length non-resident transactions exceeds C$1,000,000 in a taxation year. A Country-by-Country Report is mandatory where the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds €750,000,000, converted to Canadian dollars at the applicable exchange rate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not legislate an explicit Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the manner of the UAE; nevertheless, the GAAR, the s.247 reasonableness test, and the Canada-US treaty's limitation-on-benefits provision require the Alberta ULC to maintain real commercial substance—dedicated offices, payroll, active decision-making, and actual execution of game publishing activities. A nominally incorporated ULC holding digital sls IP and booking IAP revenue without genuine activity may attract recharacterization and loss of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating gross revenue derived from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, inflating deductible licensing or development costs, maintaining undisclosed offshore vault accounts, or filing a false T2 return; also deliberately failing to remit source-deductions from employees or contractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239 imposes, upon conviction, a fine of between 100% and 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, plus imprisonment up to 5 years; the CRA may separately assess a gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax and transfer-pricing penalties of 10% of the net adjustment. Civil penalties and compound interest accrue without limitation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be jointly and severally assessed for corporate unremitted source deductions under s.227.1 and may be subject to travel bans, asset seizure, civil restitution, and up to 5 years' imprisonment; piercing the corporate veil of an Alberta ULC is exceptionally easy because shareholders have unlimited liability for ULC debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Alberta ULC solely as a conduit that holds little or no staff, office space, or decision-making authority while shifting social-casino IP income from a U.S. group to avoid tax; making circular or self-cancelling loans; failing to document fees paid to/from associated enterprises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under s.245 to resettle tax, deny treaty withholding reductions, whole apportion income to the real business, and impose 10% transfer-pricing penalties on understated amounts; administrative monetary penalties can reach C$25,000 and criminal sanctions apply for willful avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the ULC to be treated as a sham may be personally liable for the corporation's tax under the 'legal personality' and unlimited liability provisions of the Alberta Business Corporations Act; directors also face involuntary billing assessments, court-ordered restitution, and potential clawback of improperly transferred assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a simulated casino / virtual slots game that is ostensibly free-to-play but provides prizes, coin packs, or any avenue for cashing out, thereby constituting real gambling; or failing to register with the Alberta Gaming, Liquor & Cannabis (AGLC) and failing to maintain AML programs for player payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed gaming in Alberta can trigger AGLC administrative penalties up to C$100,000 and revocation; the Criminal Code and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) expose the corporation to fines of up to C$2,000,000, asset seizure, and prosecution of officer; failure to file Currency Transaction Reports and terrorist financing reports separately attracts penalties under the PCMLTFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the PCMLTFA, directors and senior officers can be convicted personally where they were knowingly involved, incurring fines up to C$1,000,000, imprisonment up to 5 years, director disqualification, and restitution orders; in an unlimited liability company, the individual shareholders of the ULC are also directly liable for regulatory debts if the entity is unable to pay.
